canonical_spec.title: Bond cash flows and yield curves
canonical_spec.outcome: Price cash flows with spot discount factors and distinguish yield conventions.

assignments.scope: Full dated bond-cash-flow valuation. Define coupons, principal/amortization, entitlement and settlement; clean/dirty and explicitly chosen accrual/day counts; positive spot discount factors and linear replication; triangular bootstrap with rejection of inconsistent prices; YTM convention/domain/uniqueness and lack of guaranteed holding return; annual/periodic/continuous spot and forward identities with executable forward loan replication. Distinguish negative rates from arbitrage, interpolated curves from identified discount points, and discount curves from forecasts. At least three fully worked cases and ten solved graduate exercises including a proof and a substantive source/model critique.

canonical_spec.title: Duration, convexity and immunization
canonical_spec.outcome: Derive rate sensitivity and construct hedges with explicit residual risks.

assignments.scope: Derive Macaulay and modified duration and convexity from precisely stated annual/periodic price functions, with clean/dirty and units/horizon conventions. Develop portfolio dollar sensitivities, parallel first/second-order error and exact repricing; define key-rate interpolation/bump basis and show nonparallel residual risk. Derive asset-liability immunization conditions and a clearly conditional local result, with actual budgets/holdings and cash/reinvestment assumptions. Include failure examples under curve twist, large shifts, changed cash flows or rebalancing/financing costs. Three substantial worked examples minimum; ten graduate exercises with full proofs/solutions and research/model critique. A compact reproducible lab must price and test hedges independently, not present duration as universal loss protection.

canonical_spec.title: Term-structure models and rate risk
canonical_spec.outcome: Compare curve models and distinguish physical from risk-neutral dynamics.

assignments.scope: Term-structure economic expectations and time-varying risk premiums; distinguish physical conditional forecasts from risk-neutral pricing and today's implied forward rates. Derive an original finite short-rate tree with dated bank-account numeraire, backward bond valuation, positive conditional pricing probabilities/state prices, and a consistent initial curve fit. Show exactly what curve calibration identifies and what volatility/dynamics it leaves open; repricing across altered tree/curve scenarios and a hedge/model-risk example. Compare short-rate model families with assumptions and negative-rate/mean-reversion boundaries, but no reliance on Ito calculus or a continuous-time formula not yet taught. If continuous Vasicek/CIR are introduced, explain their formal scope and defer stochastic-calculus valuation to c07/c08; finite discrete models must substantively accomplish the outcome now. At least three fully worked examples and ten fully solved graduate exercises including proof/derivation and source/model critique; complete offline tree/calibration lab.

canonical_spec.title: Credit risk and recovery
canonical_spec.outcome: Value defaultable claims and separate hazard, recovery and liquidity assumptions.

assignments.scope: Credit spreads versus default, recovery, risk premium and liquidity under explicit currency/collateral contracts. Derive finite-state structural debt=min(asset value, face) and equity residual using positive pricing state weights, with physical versus pricing default probabilities; no reliance on untaught Black-Scholes. Develop survival and hazard/intensity from conditional default probabilities, exponential survival and explicitly timed recovery-of-par or other named recovery conventions; derive applicable constant-rate valuation by integration already taught. Include default absorbing transition matrices and horizon compounding, joint-default correlation/dependence with consistent marginal probabilities and tranche/portfolio loss consequences. Show nonidentification of hazard/recovery/liquidity from one spread and assumption-sensitive calibration. Three substantial worked examples minimum; ten solved graduate exercises with proof/derivation and research/model critique; original bounded reproducible credit lab. Current legal rules and real credit quotes are out of scope unless actually sourced and dated.
